Guest Issue Triage · Guest complaints, solutions & expected profit

Sample data: data/hotel_index.js was not found, so this page is showing synthetic demo hotels (DEMO-*). Figures are fabricated for UI development.

Guest complaints ranked by Stay Score per $1k

Ranked by Stay Score gained per $1,000 a year, using this hotel's own model. Profit = owner profit from the Stay Score gain; ROI = (profit − cost) ÷ cost.

How expected profit is computed
  1. Stay Score gain of a solution = this hotel's own regression (Model B) gain for the complaint's topic — the prevent gain for Prevent solutions, the resolve gain for Resolve solutions — × the assumed solution effect × the share of guests in the target audience, converted at 30.2 Stay Score points per rating point.
  2. Stay Score per $1k = Stay Score gain ÷ annual cost × 1,000. Complaints are ranked by their best solution on this metric; a complaint's solutions are ranked the same way.
  3. RevPAR / revenue gain = Stay Score gain translated through the hotel-class price elasticity applied to rooms revenue.
  4. Expected profit (owner $/yr) = rate flow-through + profit on extra room-nights + ancillary margin. The small low–high range beneath each figure brackets the assumptions.
  5. Net profit = expected profit − annual cost (unit cost × annual uses). ROI = net profit ÷ annual cost.
  6. Cost: . Hourly wages by department:
  7. Per case (one guest complaint fixed): cases / yr = complaints this solution fixes a year — per-complaint solutions: annual uses × effect; per-guest and per-room-per-year solutions: the hotel's complaints scaled to all stays × the audience's share of complaints × effect. Cost / case = annual cost ÷ cases / yr (for per-complaint solutions ≈ unit cost ÷ effect: the cost per case actually fixed). Stay Score / case = Stay Score gain ÷ cases / yr. Profit / case = expected profit ÷ cases / yr; Net / case = profit / case − cost / case. Guest rating lift = the rating change (1–5 scale) for the one guest whose case is fixed: this hotel's Model B weight for the case type (resolution weight for Resolve, prevention weight for Prevent; 0 if not positive) × the solution effect.
  8. "Fixing it entirely" = the Stay Score the hotel would gain if this complaint disappeared completely (Model B gain for the topic at 100% effect, all guests).
  9. Each solution is listed once, for the one audience it targets (family solutions are for Families only; general solutions are for All guests). Solutions for one complaint overlap, so they are alternatives, not additive.
  10. Urgent complaints are pinned at the very top, then Safety & security complaints ("Safety · escalate"): both go to Security / GM regardless of cost or rank.
  11. Several guest complaints can map to the same case type (model topic). They share one set of numbers, because the model scores the case type, not the wording.
Disclosures:
  • Historical rating association; not causal
  • Default cost/effect values are editable assumptions
  • Candidate coverage is not full classification accuracy
  • Safety/legal items override cost ranking
